text:
alex: seeing a mini eviction wave in apse1-azb since 02:12 UTC, lots of tiny pods stuck Pending and GPU warm nodes not handing out slots. strange heatmap in packer too.
maria: yup saw it, warm-node heartbeats spiked and some nodes hit thermal throttle, kubelet started refusing attaches. logs: 
```
Mar 03 02:11:58 node-azb-47 kubelet: attach/detach controller error: attach failed: device not ready
Mar 03 02:12:01 node-azb-47 kubelet: thermal_alert: GPU throttle high, entering cooldown
```
jeff: any correlation with recent rack firmware push? ops-bot: ALERT apse1-azb: gpu-thermal-throttle-rate > 0.2 (30m)
rina: if warm nodes go into cooldown they don't advertise slots -> scheduler sees fragmentation and tries to evict to other racks => cascade. We should avoid global reschedule.
alex: suggestion: temporarily disable cross-az gangbackfill for this rack while we triage, and bump warmpool size by 2 nodes for azb only. low blast radius label approach.
maria: +1. quick command to label racks for canary: `kubectl label node -l rack=azb warmpool-canary=true` then patch autoscaler config to target `warmpool-canary=true` pool.
jeff: cost note — bumping warmpool by 2 for an hour is ~+$220/hr. ok for a mitigation window?
alex: fine. prefer cheap mitigation vs mass requeues. also we should relax `topologySpreadConstraints` on tiny pods for 30m so scheduler can pack them in non-throttled nodes within the same az.
rina: risky to relax constraints globally. do it only for the affected deployment(s): `kubectl patch deploy small-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"temp-pack-relax":"true"}}}}}'` and adapter reads that.
sre-oncall: I'm going to cordon node-azb-47 and drain any evicted-resident pods to avoid churn while we patch autoscaler. `kubectl cordon node-azb-47` `kubectl drain node-azb-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
maria: after cordon, I see scheduler backlog drop in 2m. telemetry: `pack_frag_score` dropped from 0.78 -> 0.34 after the canary warmpool increased.
jeff: nice. keep an eye on cross-az egress — we don't want to create network hotspots.
alex: noted. also filing follow-up to investigate firmware delta. if thermal triggers are spiking, could be a driver regression or fan curve change.
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0311-azb-thermal. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0311-azb-thermal
maria: plan: 1) apply warmpool canary +2 nodes 2) label and relax small-worker spreads for 30m 3) monitor pack_frag_score & evict rate 4) rollback in 1h or when stable 5) open infra ticket for firmware/drivers
jeff: SGTM. please annotate the rollout in the deploy log and estimate cost in the ticket.
sre-oncall: executing step 1 & 2 now. will ping when done.
alex: thanks — ping once pack_frag_score < 0.4 and evictions < 5/min. :thumbsup:
maria: done. warmpool scaled, labels applied, backlog dropping.
sre-oncall: drain finished on node-azb-47. requeueing only system pods.
jeff: after 12m, evictions back to baseline. keep watch for 45m then rollback scale.
alex: created temp cost/ops tag on the project for the bump.
maria: adding a short eval to detect thermal spikes and auto-flag warmpool adjustments for next time (alert threshold proposal in ticket).
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-2026-0311-azb-thermal — mitigated, monitoring.
jeff: nice team work. follow-up: schedule a root-cause session tomorrow with infra/firmware teams.
alex: ACK. :wave:
